verdict.why: Against the brief’s ordered criteria, X is the spec a zero-context implementer can build without asking. Criterion 1: the owner asked for taken, one backlog row, and a date — X Rollout steps 4–5 and Decisions Q2 give one row and 2026-12-07 / 2026-12-21, keep the matrix at scenarios × personas, leave agent-tester byte-identical (REQ-12), and consume the stated facts (door test-stand.sshlg, key per sender, never on the command line) in C8. The six hard cells in C2 match the 2026-11-23 study (RTL, double-length, largest text, dark, small screen, tablet). Criterion 2: C1–C7 plus T-01–T-22 fix grammars, exit codes, and the stand check (local stand-captures/1 manifest, cell config equality, SHA-256, --build). Criterion 3: one-config-per-persona, derived dir, gap-gating, and schema staying design-review/1 are decided with rejected alternatives; unknowns Q5–Q6 are isolated to phase 2 so phase 1 is not blocked. Y misses the required date (Goal: dates are the owner’s; Q1 answer is only “next minor release”, by pending), pushes line syntax and JSON names to pending Q3–Q13, and its report gate never checks cell equality, capture bytes, or hashes (R11/C5–C6 only require non-empty run/cell/build). That is more questions and a part 2 that cannot be verified. Y’s separate dir axis and “yes blocked on a gap” (R9) are better readings of “language and direction” and “only in this configuration”, but they do not outweigh a spec the implementer cannot close.
risks: X Design stand-intake step 4 refuses untagged explore screenshots, which can cancel the brief’s “explore or scripted runs” path if cells are not tagged with design-review scenario ids — a join the facts never state.

Direction is derived from a fixed script/language list rather than stored, so the owner’s “language and direction” column can be wrong for locales outside that list; the list is unsupported invention.
The realization table writes unconfirmed xcrun/adb/browser flags into references/design-review.md (Q9). Wrong flags become doctrine and rework.
Phase 2 fetch is explicitly not buildable until Q5/Q6, yet the reply dates claim stand intake; CFG-STAND-NOBUILD is only a warning, so stand rows can pass with no --build.
C2’s Config declined line waives a hard cell, so the six stress configurations are not actually mandatory. REQ-5 also assumes --require build/design, which the brief’s facts never name.
